summaries.summary: December events include the Christmas Party on the 12th at 6:00 pm at Ivy Grove and the Annual Norwegian Bake Sale on the 14th at the Legion, with members donating goods or paying a fee. Current officers are Karen Fried (President), David Peterson (Vice President), Vernon Roble (Counselor), Kati Peterson (Secretary), Loretta Knutson (Treasurer), and others.

September's meeting features a program on WWII Belgium memories, while October has no regular meeting but a planned bus trip to Westby on October 29th. A bus trip to Plymouth for a play on August 14th is full, departing at 7:30 AM, and the August Pot Luck Picnic hosted guests from Nor-Win Lodge.

The January meeting features Elaine Hegg discussing her book "Death in a One-Room Country School" with soup and finger food provided by members, followed by a business meeting. The annual Norwegian Bake Sale occurred on December 14th, and the 15th Annual Barnelopet is scheduled for February 1st in Decorah. The Sons of Norway District 1 Convention is set for June 12-14, 2014, in Duluth, MN.

July's monthly meeting featuring Howard Sherpe will occur on July 10th at the Spring Grove Legion. The July 15th Book Club meeting and July 30th Board Meeting are also upcoming. For August, members are invited to Nor-Win Lodge in Winona on the 26th for a picnic, and volunteers are needed for Meals on Wheels the week of August 4th, with Judy and Janet already committed.

Monthly meetings are scheduled for March 8 and April 10. The annual Flatbread Day is on April 19 and open to the public, while Syttende Mai celebrations are planned for May 16-18. The 2014 Norwegian Language Camp runs June 9-13 and June 16-20, with scholarships available.

For May 17th, the Lodge will celebrate Syttende Mai at the Legion with a Bake Sale, demonstrations, and a boat parade. Upcoming events include a Board Meeting on June 4th, a monthly Show & Tell on June 12th, a Book Club road trip on June 17th, and a visit from Kristiana Lodge on June 28th. The Norwegian Ridge Language Camp runs June 9-13 and 16-20, with Lodge scholarships available.

November meeting on the 13th includes updates and an election call for Secretary and Vice President. Upcoming events include a Christmas party on the 11th, a Norwegian bake sale on the 13th, and book club meetings on the 18th and 16th.

Sept/October 2014 is winding down. Key upcoming events include the October 4 UFF DA FEST Bake Sale at the Heritage Center, the October 9 meeting featuring Westby Lodge guests, and the December 11 Christmas Party. The newsletter also congratulates members Morris and Geneva Tweeten on their 65th anniversary and Ragnhild St. Mary on her 100th birthday, while recognizing Lee Grippen's volunteer service.

The first meeting of 2015 is scheduled for January 10th at the Giants of the Earth Heritage Center, featuring Ron and Freida Nowland and a soup lunch. The annual Barnelopet children's ski event will take place on February 7th in Decorah. Recent announcements include the December 11th meeting at Ivy Grove restaurant and the lodge's Annual Norwegian Bake Sale held on December 13th.

July's newsletter highlights the upcoming Potluck Picnic with Solvang Lodge on Tuesday, July 28th, followed by a Board Meeting on August 5th. August features a program with NorWin Lodge on the 13th about Gudrid and a Book Club meeting on the 18th, while Syttende Mai was recently celebrated successfully. The newsletter also announces the Norsk Høstfest (Sept 29-3) and Decorah's Nordic Fest (July 24-6).

The March meeting features a history talk on Norwegian carriage decoration. Upcoming events include an April 9 visit to Lanesboro Lodge, a public "Flatbread Day" on April 11, a reception for the Norwegian immigration exhibit on April 19, and the May 17-19 Syttende Mai celebrations with bake sales.

Valheim Lodge's May/June 2015 newsletter highlights upcoming events including the Syttende Mai Royalty Tea on May 9th, the May Regular Monthly Meeting featuring David Glomstad on May 14th, and the Spring Grove SYTTENDE MAI Fest on May 16th, which includes a Bake Sale, demonstrations, and a Grand Parade starting at 1:30 pm. The newsletter also lists current officers and encourages members to participate in lodge activities, including the annual boat parade.

Upcoming events include the November 12 meeting featuring guest speaker Blaine Hedberg and updates on the Christmas party and bake sale, the December 2 board meeting, the December 10 Christmas party with a $10/person cost and sign-up required, and the December 19 bake sale where members can donate baked goods or $20. The Tuesday, November 17 book club meeting is also scheduled.

Key upcoming events include the September 15 Book Club discussion of "Unbroken", the September 30 Board Meeting, the UFF DA FEST Bake Sale on October 3 at the Heritage Center (members bring donated baked goods), the October 8 Monthly Meeting featuring WWII POW stories, the November 12 Monthly Meeting, and the December 10 Christmas Party. The newsletter also announces congratulations and condolences for members, notes upcoming Lodge meetings, and provides details about past events like the Westby Day Trip and July meeting.

The first meeting of 2016 is January 9th at 11 a.m. at the Giants of the Earth Heritage Center, followed by the annual Barnelopet on February 6th in Decorah. Founders' Day is January 16th, and the full schedule of meetings includes dates throughout the year, with a December meeting already held.

Valheim Lodge's July/August 2016 newsletter highlights upcoming events including a meeting with Solvang Lodge on Tuesday, July 26th at 6 PM, a board meeting on Wednesday, August 3rd at 11 AM, a social gathering at NorWin Lodge on Tuesday, August 23rd at 6 PM, and a book club meeting on Wednesday, August 16th at 2 PM. The newsletter also notes the successful conclusion of the June Syttende Mai celebration and announces the ongoing planning for the new Oslo Viking Age Museum.

The March monthly meeting is scheduled for March 12th featuring a presentation on Norwegian sweaters by Laurann Gilbertson. Upcoming events include a potential day trip to Vesterheim on April 7th, a visit from Lanesboro Lodge on the 14th, the annual Flatbread Day on April 16th (free and open to the public), and the Syttende Mai celebration from May 20-22 involving a bake sale and demonstrations.

May 12th features a regular meeting with a Norwegian Constitution anniversary program at the Legion. Upcoming Syttende Mai events include a May 14th Royalty Tea, May 17th-20th Giants of the Earth and Spring Grove Fest with a parade on the 20th, and a bake sale.

The Valheim Lodge newsletter highlights the upcoming December 8 Christmas Party at the Heritage Center (buffet, $10 meal fee, no gift exchange, holiday sing-along) and the December 17 Norwegian Bake Sale (baked goods or donation). The November 10 meeting will feature a speaker on the 1940 Armistice Day Blizzard and include the election of 2017 officers. Current officers include Karen Fried (President), Thomas Trehus (VP), Jillelyn Stolie (Secretary), Loretta Knutson (Treasurer & Membership), and Lee Grippen (Social/Cultural).

October 1 will feature the UFF DA FEST Bake Sale at the Giants of the Earth Heritage Center. The lodge's Recruitment Challenge is ongoing through the year, and December 8 will host the Christmas Party, with the Annual Norwegian Bake Sale at the SG Legion on December 17.

The Valheim Lodge January meeting featured presentations from Jill Storlie and Jackie Parker, followed by a "Souper Saturday" soup potluck lunch. Key upcoming events include the February 11th Norwegian Stabbur Story program and the annual Barnelopet children's ski event on February 4th.

The March monthly meeting features Lee Grippen discussing his experiences with Norwegian exchange students. April events include a carpool to Lanesboro, the annual Flatbread Day on April 22nd, a Learn Laugh Eat recipe booklet deadline by April 15th, and the 20th Annual Ibsen Festival from April 21-23rd. Sons of Norway dues will increase starting August 2017.

Key upcoming events include a Syttende Mai Barnetoget (Children's Parade) on Wednesday, May 17, featuring hot dogs at the park, and a Syttende Mai/Homecoming Royalty Tea on Saturday, May 13, at the Heritage Center. Homecoming will take place on Saturday, June 24, with a morning bake sale, demonstrations, and a boat parade. Notable dates also include Oranda Sinclair's 90th birthday on May 12 and Janet Fossum's 90th birthday on May 12.

The December Christmas Party is scheduled for Thursday, December 14th, featuring a buffet meal, White Elephant gift exchange, and sing-along. The Norwegian Bake Sale, the lodge's main fundraiser, will take place on Saturday, December 16th at the Heritage Center. The current officers include Karen Fried as President and Loretta Knutson as Treasurer.

September 14 features a regular meeting on spirits and sheep, followed by a tour of Rock Filter Distillery. October 7 hosts a Kaffe Fest, a coffee-themed fundraiser with donations. The December 14 Christmas Party and December 16 Annual Bake Sale are upcoming social events. The newsletter also announces the upcoming implementation of simplified dues for 2018 starting January 1.

The Valheim Lodge newsletter highlights several upcoming events for 2018, including monthly meetings featuring speakers like Miranda Moen (Jan 6) and Tim Kindseth (Feb 10), all held at the Giants of the Earth Heritage Center. Other notable events include the Highland Voices musical program (March 10), the Barnelopet children's ski/walk event (Feb 3), and various themed programs throughout the year. The newsletter also announces the need for volunteers for the 2018 officer elections and mentions the opportunity to send a delegate to the District One Convention in June.

The lodge highlights the upcoming Decorah's Nordic Fest from July 26-28 and the Norsk Høstfest from September 26-29. They also announce the Matlyst Monthly meeting featuring meatballs in gjetost sauce.

March's monthly meeting featured the returning Highland Voices, while April's gathering included a program by Glenn Borreson and an evening meeting at the Legion. The annual Flatbread Day is scheduled for April 21st, and members are encouraged to submit recipes for the upcoming Learn, Laugh, Eat! booklet by April 12th.

This newsletter highlights several upcoming Norwegian celebrations. Key events include a Syttende Mai Royalty Tea on May 12, the annual Syttende Mai celebration with a bake sale and parade on May 19, and a May Monthly Meeting on May 10. Additionally, the newsletter congratulates member Lee Grippen on receiving the Order of St. Olav medal.

December Christmas Party and BAKE SALE will be held on Thursday, December 13th at the Heritage Center. The Norwegian Bake Sale occurs the following Saturday, December 15th, at the same location and is the lodge's main fundraiser. Additionally, the Luren Singers will present their Christmas Concert on Sunday, December 9th at Trinity Lutheran Church.

The January meeting on January 12th featured a "Mushrooms...Delicious or Deadly?" program and a Souper Saturday lunch, with officers serving as the first person committee. The December meeting was the lodge's Christmas party, which included a free meal, a White Elephant gift exchange, and music. The annual Norwegian Bake Sale was held on December 15th and was a huge success.

July meetings feature a joint gathering with Westby Lodge on July 25th at the La Crescent Fire Hall for a reenactment and BBQ potluck, followed by an August 8th meeting hosting Winona Lodge at the Heritage Center for a murder mystery program. The Lodge is planning a 90th anniversary celebration for November and encourages members to bring collected Tubfrim stamps or food shelf items to monthly meetings.

April meetings include a guest night at Lanesboro Lodge on April 4 and a presentation on Norwegian history on May 9. Key events are Flatbread Day on April 27, the May 11 Mollie B show, the May 17 Barnetoget parade, and the May 18 Syttende Mai celebration. Additionally, the lodge is offering $50 scholarships to members' children for the upcoming Norwegian Ridge Language & Culture Camp in June.

May 17 features a Barnetoget (children's parade) with hot dog/lefses provided by the lodge, followed by the May 18 Syttende Mai celebration including a bake sale, boat parade, and various events. The June 13 monthly meeting will feature Joe Morken discussing his trip to Norway, and the lodge promotes its annual Norwegian Ridge Language Camp with member scholarships.

The September meeting featured Norwegian woodcarving. The October 5th Kaffe Fest coincided with Uff Da Fest. The Lodge's 90th Anniversary is planned for November 17th, and Sons of Norway will celebrate its 125th anniversary in 2020.

The January meeting features a program on ice by Dennis Barnaal and a Souper Saturday soup donation/lunch, held January 18 at the Heritage Center. The lodge celebrated its 90th anniversary in November with a Luren Singers concert and fellowship lunch. A successful December bake sale and Audrey Almo's birthday celebration also occurred, along with the announcement of the annual Barnelopet children's ski/walk event scheduled for February 1.

Monthly meetings are scheduled for March 14, April 4, and May 14, featuring presentations and guest speakers. The May 15-17 Syttende Mai celebration includes various events, and the lodge is coordinating participation. The District Convention for electing delegates is June 4-6, 2020, at Cragun's Resort, with registration deadlines and costs specified.

Valheim Lodge held a successful Viking Fest in November 2022, welcoming new members and using a $900 Lodge Vitality Grant. They are also hosting a Norwegian Bake Sale on December 17th and a Christmas Party on December 28th, both at the Giants of the Earth Heritage Center.

May 17th offers a monthly meeting and the Barnetoget children's parade, followed by a May 14th bake sale/demonstration and the Spring Grove Syttende Mai celebration. June 21st marks the Midsommer meeting, and the lodge is planning a vitality event in late November to encourage new membership.

The next Sons of Norway Lodge Vitality Event is tentatively planned for Sunday, November 6, 2022, aiming to engage members and the public with Viking-themed activities. Upcoming lodge meetings include an August gathering in Winona and a September program featuring the Viking story illustrated with world stamps. Additionally, the UFF DA FEST is scheduled for Saturday, October 8.

The December lodge meeting featured a Yulebukker guessing game, a White Elephant gift exchange, and a bake sale raising over $400. A program by Karla Brown shared family photos from Norway in 1908, and a survey revealed krumkaker as the favorite Norwegian Christmas cookie. The January meeting will include the Fødselsdagskringle recipe and feature the lodge's officers.

July 27th meeting in LaCrescent features a potluck supper and guest speaker Chris Hardie. June meeting will discuss the lodge's book club and Sports Medals Program. The lodge was active during Syttende Mai week with multiple community events.

Community members are invited to the May 16 baking event featuring Norwegian treats. The Barnetoget parade and Maypole activities will take place on May 17, with volunteers needed for lefse service. Sons of Norway members are strongly encouraged to volunteer for the upcoming May 20 "Taste of Norway" Middag meal and food demonstrations, with sign-ups available online.

Valheim Lodge's December newsletter highlights the upcoming November 28 Book Club meeting featuring "Keeping Christmas" and a December 2 monthly meeting with a Christmas party, featuring Norwegian traditions and a potluck meal. The newsletter also shares a recipe for Trøndersodd, a traditional Trøndelag dish, and reflects on past lodge activities.

Proposed monthly meetings for January through June are scheduled for Saturdays at 11:00 a.m. (Jan, Feb, March) and Thursdays at 6:00 p.m. (April, May, June), with locations in Spring Grove except for April in Lanesboro. The Lodge is planning to co-sponsor the Taste of Norway event for Syttende Mai and potentially host a Hotdish Contest at Uff Da Fest, while the December Christmas party date is still undecided.

The Bake Sale during Syttende Mai was a huge success, raising over $1,000, and the parade boat ride was enjoyed by many, with thanks to Audrey Almo for the accordion music and Jim & Karen Gray for pulling the boat. The elementary students participated in the Barnetoget, receiving treats at Viking Memorial Park, thanks to volunteers including Bill Fried, Audrey Almo, Gretchen Anderson, and Nora Beckjord. Upcoming events include the July meeting in La Crescent featuring Kevin Doely (a ventriloquist) and a potluck dinner, with a carpool option available.

The March 9 meeting features David Engen discussing his experience on "Alt for Norge." An April 4 meeting with Heimbygde Lodge is planned, likely involving a carpool. Additionally, a bus trip is being considered for the April 23 Norway House event during Spring Grove Day.

The November monthly meeting featuring Dale Goodman on the Restoration will be held on November 9th at Giants of the Earth Heritage Center. The December monthly meeting, which is the Annual Sons of Norway event, will take place on December 14th at the same location. The lodge is also hosting a Christmas party on December 13th at Giants of the Earth Heritage Center.

Valheim Lodge celebrated receiving Gold Merit Certificates at the District 1 convention in August and was recognized as the 2023 Family Lodge of the Year (Small Lodge). Upcoming meetings feature woodcarving and Norwegian-themed programs by Rebecca Hanna and Miranda Moen in September and October, both featuring potluck meals. The lodge is also hosting events at the Uff Da Fest, including a Kaffe Mat coffee and Norwegian treats on October 4th and a Hot Dish Contest on October 6th.

July's meeting is on Tuesday, July 22nd at 5:30 pm in La Crescent featuring Laughter Yoga with Laura Gentry. August's meeting on Thursday, August 14th includes a road trip to Houston to hear Shelley Jerviss at the museum. The lodge is also announcing adult scholarships for Norwegian language/culture study starting in August 2025.

Hosts are needed for upcoming monthly meetings, with scheduled dates listed (March 8, April 12, May 8, June 12, July 22, August 14, September 11, October 11, November 8). March's meeting features a presentation on Norway by Finn Brobakken, while April's meeting welcomes members from Lanesboro Lodge and includes a program on Viking crosses by Glenn Borreson.

The upcoming Syttende Mai Festival will be held May 14-18, with key events including the Barnetoget on May 16 and a parade on May 17. Valheim Lodge's May monthly meeting is on May 8 at Giants of the Earth, featuring a program on Norwegian children's literature. Janet Fossum's 98th birthday is on May 12, and members are encouraged to send her birthday cards.

September/October events include Glenn Kinneberg's talk on September 11th and Rolf Svanoe's presentation on October 11th, alongside the Uff Da Fest from October 3rd-5th featuring Kaffe Mat on the 4th and the third annual Hot Dish Contest on the 5th. The Sons of Norway Valheim Lodge also announces the ongoing progress of the Norwegian ship Restauration's Atlantic voyage and the upcoming premiere of the documentary "Dear Land" at the Spring Grove Cinema on November 1st.

July 25 meeting with Solvang Lodge in LaCrosse (potluck, carpool), August 2 board meeting in Ivy Grove, and August 10 meeting with Winona Lodge at Trinity Lutheran Church (potluck, featuring Rachel Storlie's music).

The next regular lodge meeting is Thursday, September 13, featuring a program on Norwegian folk art, and the following Thursday, October 11, will focus on growing up in Norway. Don't miss the upcoming Kaffe Fest on Saturday, October 6, where members can donate goods for a coffee and baked goods event, and the genealogy workshop sponsored by Decorah Genealogy Association on Saturday, September 22.

The Sons of Norway Valheim Lodge is preparing for Syttende Mai celebrations over the weekend of May 17-19, featuring events including a Children's Parade (Barnetoget) on Friday, a Bake Sale and Parade on Saturday morning, and a Taste of Norway event in the evening. The Lodge also announced membership benefits, including access to dedicated life insurance professionals, and reminded members about the March meeting featuring speaker David Engen.

The lodge proposes monthly meetings for 2025, starting with a January 11th meeting featuring speakers Rachel and David Storlie and concluding with a Christmas party date still to be determined. Upcoming events include meetings with other lodges (Lanesboro, Westby, Winona) and a December potluck lunch celebrating Norwegian heritage.

Dave and Ruth Amundson will present on the Restauration 2 arrival and their History Alive organization at the November 8 meeting, followed by a potluck lunch. The December 11 Christmas Party at the Heritage Center includes a social hour, meal, Christmas songs, and a White Elephant gift exchange, not a potluck. The December meeting will focus on the Restauration ship, and the annual Uff Da Fest Hot Dish Contest saw wins by Sue Scobie, Jean Young, and Sheila Livingstone.

Valheim Lodge is commemorating its 90th Anniversary with a special event on Sunday, November 17th, featuring a concert by the Luren Singing Society, a slide show, and a light luncheon at Trinity Lutheran Church, asking members for help and donations. Following this, the Lodge is hosting its annual December Christmas Party on Thursday, December 12th, with a buffet meal and gift exchange, and a Norwegian Bake Sale on Saturday, December 14th.
